lines.say: There's a terrifying detail on this violin,
and it explains why the painter stopped to listen.
This is Self-Portrait with Death Playing the Fiddle,
painted by Arnold Böcklin in 1872.
A bearded painter holds his brush,
and behind him a skeleton plays the violin.
But look at the violin.
It has only one string.
The painter doesn't turn. The painter doesn't run.
He simply listens.
According to Alma Mahler,
her husband Gustav wrote his Fourth Symphony
under the spell of this picture.
A violin should have four strings.
But Böcklin gave Death a fiddle with one.
And here's the disturbing part.
Death has only one string,
yet the painter cannot stop listening.
As if the song ends when that string breaks.
Maybe the last string is his own life.
So is the painter working,
or listening to his own end?
